Four friends are stuck on the wrong side of a canyon, at night.
The old bridge holds only two people at a time, and they have just one torch.
No one can cross without the torch, so someone has to carry it back each time.
They cross at different speeds: one, two, five, and ten minutes. A pair moves at the slower person's pace.
In seventeen minutes, the bridge collapses. Can they all make it?
Most people let the fastest friend walk everyone across, one by one.
Ten, plus one, plus five, plus one, plus two. That's nineteen minutes. Too slow!
The trick: send the two slowest across together, so their times overlap.
First, one and two cross. Two minutes.
One brings the torch back. Three minutes.
Now five and ten cross together. Thirteen minutes.
Two brings the torch back. Fifteen minutes.
And one and two cross again. Seventeen minutes, exactly!
Everyone's safe, just as the bridge falls.
